questions.q: C is described as which kind of programming language?
choices: Imperative and procedural: a sequence of statements, organized into functions
Object-oriented: programs are organized into classes and objects
Functional: programs are built only from expressions with no statements
Interpreted scripting: programs run inside a virtual machine
questions.explain: A C program is a sequence of statements (imperative) structured as a set of functions, also called procedures (procedural).

questions.q: C has built-in support for object-oriented programming, like Python, Java, and C++.
questions.explain: C is less abstracted from machine language and does not support object-oriented programming.

questions.q: You need a dictionary (key-value map) data structure in a C program. What do you do?
choices: Use C's built-in dict literal syntax {key: value}
Declare a variable of type map
questions.explain: C does not provide high-level abstractions like strings, lists, or dictionaries, so you have to implement a dictionary yourself.

questions.q: Which of these are reasons C is still the main language for systems programming?
choices: Programmers get more control over how their programs manage memory
C code can run more efficiently than equivalent code that uses higher-level abstractions
It is easier to see the relationship between the code and how the computer executes it
C provides a rich set of built-in data structures such as lists and dictionaries
C programs run on an interpreter that acts as a virtual machine
questions.explain: C is close to the machine, so it gives control and efficiency, especially over memory. It has no built-in lists or dictionaries, and it is compiled, not interpreted.

questions.q: C translates relatively straightforwardly into the assembly and machine code that a computer executes.
questions.explain: Because C is less abstracted from the machine, its translation to assembly and machine code is relatively direct.

questions.q: How is a multiline comment written in C?
questions.explain: C multiline comments begin with /* and end with */. Python uses ''' for multiline comments.

questions.q: What two characters start a single-line comment in C?
questions.explain: In C, a single-line comment begins with //. Python uses # instead.

questions.q: Which line correctly brings the standard I/O library into a C program?
questions.explain: C includes libraries with #include. These lines go at the top of the program, outside any function body.

questions.q: In C, indentation determines which statements belong to a block.
questions.explain: Indentation has no meaning in C. Blocks are marked with { and }. Indenting by nesting level is still good style.

questions.q: How are blocks such as function, loop, and conditional bodies marked in C?
choices: They start with { and end with }
They start with begin and end with end
They start with a colon (:) and end with a blank line
questions.explain: C blocks start with { and end with }.

questions.q: What marks the end of a statement in C?
questions.explain: Every C statement ends with a semicolon. Line breaks do not separate statements.

questions.q: You forget the semicolon at the end of line 5 of a C program. Where does gcc often report the syntax error?
choices: On line 6, the line after the missing semicolon
On line 5, with the message "missing semicolon"
On line 1, at the start of the file
Nowhere; the compiler adds the semicolon automatically
questions.explain: gcc reads the next line as part of the unfinished statement, so the error usually shows up on the line after. gcc almost never says directly that a semicolon is missing.

questions.q: In C, a statement such as printf("hi\n"); may appear at the top level of a file, outside every function.
questions.explain: C statements must be inside the body of some function.

questions.q: In the definition int main(void) { ... }, what does void mean?
choices: main does not expect to receive any parameters
main does not return a value
main runs automatically in the background
questions.explain: void in the parameter list means main takes no parameters. The int before main is its return type.

questions.q: What return type must a C program's main function have?
choices: Any type, chosen by the programmer
questions.explain: A C program must have a function named main, and its return type must be int (a signed integer).

questions.q: By convention, what value should main return when the program runs to completion without errors?
questions.explain: main returns 0 to signal successful completion without error.

questions.q: As in Python, a C program needs an explicit call to main() before main will run.
questions.explain: C calls main automatically when the program starts. A Python program needs an explicit call such as main().

questions.q: C's printf automatically prints a newline at the end of its output, the same way Python's print does.
questions.explain: printf does not add a newline. You have to put \n in the format string when you want one.

questions.q: In printf("sqrt(4) is %f\n", sqrt(4)); how is the value for the %f placeholder supplied?
choices: As an additional argument to printf, after a comma
After a % symbol that follows the format string
Inside the format string, in curly braces
Through a separate call to format()
questions.explain: In C, placeholder values are extra comma-separated arguments to printf. Python's % formatting puts the values after a % symbol.

questions.q: Which statement correctly contrasts how Python and C programs are run?
choices: Python is run by an interpreter program; C must first be compiled into a binary executable that the system runs directly
Both are compiled into binary executables before they run
Both are run directly by an interpreter
C is run by an interpreter; Python must be compiled first
questions.explain: The Python interpreter, itself a binary executable, runs hello.py. A C compiler translates hello.c into a binary executable that the OS and hardware run directly.

questions.q: What is a binary executable?
choices: A series of 0s and 1s in a well-defined format that the computer can run directly
A C source file that has been saved with a .c suffix
A text file of assembly instructions that an interpreter reads
A list of the libraries a program includes
questions.explain: A binary executable is 0s and 1s in a well-defined format that the hardware and OS can execute directly. A compiler produces one from source code.

questions.q: You run gcc hello.c without other options and compilation succeeds. What is the default name of the executable file it creates?
questions.explain: By default, gcc names the binary executable a.out.

questions.q: Which command compiles hello.c into an executable named hello?
questions.explain: The -o flag sets the output file name: gcc -o <output_executable_file> <input_source_file>.

questions.q: On a Unix system, how do you run an executable named hello that is in the current directory?
questions.explain: Use ./hello to run the executable in the current directory.

questions.q: Some C compilers have to be told explicitly to link in the math library. What gcc option does this (as in gcc hello.c ____)?
questions.explain: gcc hello.c -lm links in the math library.

questions.q: In gcc -Wall -g -o hello hello.c, what do the -Wall and -g options add?
choices: More compiler warnings, plus extra debugging information in the executable
Faster code, plus a smaller executable
Automatic linking of all libraries, plus a debugger that starts automatically
Warnings treated as errors, plus generated assembly output
questions.explain: These options turn on more compiler warnings (-Wall) and build the executable with extra debugging information (-g).

questions.q: You edit hello.c, and the new gcc -o hello hello.c fails with errors. Any older ./hello from an earlier successful build is guaranteed to be deleted.
questions.explain: A failed compile does not create or re-create ./hello, but an older version from an earlier successful build may still be there. Running it would run the old code.

questions.q: After you change hello.c, you must recompile it with gcc before ./hello reflects the change.
questions.explain: The executable is built from the source. Any change to the source needs a recompile to produce a new executable.

questions.q: Which utility is often used to simplify long gcc commands and to clean up files that gcc creates?
questions.explain: The make utility, driven by a Makefile, is commonly used to compile C programs and to clean up generated files.

questions.q: In C, every variable must be declared before it can be used.
questions.explain: C requires a declaration of the form type_name variable_name; before a variable is used.

questions.q: By convention, where should variables be declared in C?
choices: At the beginning of their scope (the top of a { } block), before any statements in that block
Immediately before the line where they are first used
At the end of the block that uses them
Only in a separate header file
questions.explain: By convention, C variables are declared at the top of their { } block, before any C statements in that scope.

questions.q: What does a variable's type define, as opposed to its scope?
choices: The range of values it can represent and how those values are interpreted in operations
Where in the program it can be used and how long it exists
The name used to refer to it
questions.explain: Type sets the range of values and how they are interpreted. Scope sets where and when the variable can be used, plus its lifetime.

questions.q: Which of these are valid C variable declarations?
questions.explain: Declarations follow type_name variable_name; and you can declare several variables of the same type at once. x int; puts the type in the wrong place, and C has no built-in string type.

questions.q: After char letter = 'A'; letter = letter + 1; what does letter hold?
choices: A compile error, because you cannot add to a char
questions.explain: A char holds a small integer, the ASCII code of the character. Adding 1 to 'A' gives the next ASCII value, which is 'B'.

questions.q: The char literal 'h' has what numeric (ASCII) value?
questions.explain: 'h' is a char literal whose value is 104, the ASCII code for h.

questions.q: In C, 'h' and "h" are the same value.
questions.explain: 'h' is a char literal with value 104. "h" is a string literal, a different type that does not evaluate to 104.

questions.q: C has a built-in string type.
questions.explain: C has no string type. Strings are built from arrays of char. C does support string literals: characters in double quotes.

questions.q: What is the type of the numeric literal 3.4 in C?
questions.explain: A literal with a decimal point such as 3.4 is a double. A literal like 8 is an int.

questions.q: What is the usual size of an int in C?
questions.explain: Usual sizes: char 1, short 2, int 4, long 4 or 8, long long 8, float 4, double 8 bytes.

questions.q: What is the usual size, in bytes, of a double in C?
questions.explain: A double is usually 8 bytes and a float is usually 4. The extra bytes give double more precision.

questions.q: Which C types store real (decimal-point) numbers?
questions.explain: float and double store signed real numbers. int and short store signed integers, and unsigned int stores nonnegative integers.

questions.q: The C standard guarantees that char is a signed type.
questions.explain: The standard does not say whether char is signed or unsigned, so implementations differ. Declare unsigned char explicitly if you want the unsigned version.

questions.q: Which C operator takes a type name and evaluates to the number of bytes used to store that type?
questions.explain: For example, sizeof(int) is usually 4. Sizes vary by architecture, so sizeof tells you the exact size on a given machine.

questions.q: sizeof evaluates to an unsigned long. Which printf placeholder should you use to print it?
questions.explain: For example: printf("number of bytes in an int: %lu\n", sizeof(int));

questions.q: In C, what does the expression 8 / 3 evaluate to?
questions.explain: When both operands are int, / does integer division and drops everything after the decimal point.

questions.q: In C, what does the expression 8 / 3.0 evaluate to (approximately)?
questions.explain: One operand is a floating-point value, so / does real division, giving about 2.666667.

questions.q: An int operand is combined with a float operand by an arithmetic operator. What happens?
choices: The int is converted to its floating-point equivalent first, and the result is a float
The float is truncated to an int first, and the result is an int
The compiler reports a type error
The result type depends on which operand comes first
questions.explain: C converts types automatically. The integer operand becomes a float before the operation, and the result is a float.

questions.q: C's mod operator (%) accepts float and double operands.
questions.explain: % only takes integer-type operands, such as int, unsigned int, and short.

questions.q: In C, what does 17 % 5 evaluate to?
questions.explain: % is the mod (remainder) operator. 17 = 3 * 5 + 2, so the result is 2.

questions.q: After int x = 20; x /= 3; what is the value of x?
questions.explain: x /= 3 is shorthand for x = x / 3. With int operands, 20 / 3 truncates to 6.

questions.q: What is x += 3; shorthand for?
questions.explain: Assignment with update (variable op= expression) is shorthand for variable = variable op expression.

questions.q: After x = 6; y = ++x + 2; what is the value of y?
questions.explain: Pre-increment: x goes to 7 first, then x + 2 is evaluated, so y is 9.

questions.q: After x = 6; y = x++ + 2; what is the value of y?
questions.explain: Post-increment: x + 2 is evaluated with x's current value (6), giving 8. Then x is incremented.

questions.q: After x = 6; y = x++ + 2; what is the value of x?
questions.explain: Post-increment uses x's value first and then increments it, so x ends up as 7.

questions.q: Written as standalone statements, x++; and ++x; have the same effect.
questions.explain: When the incremented value is not used in the same statement, pre- and post-increment both just add 1 to x. x++; is the more common form.

questions.q: You want to increment x and then assign x + 1 to y. Which is the clearest, recommended way to write it?
choices: x++; then y = x + 1; as two separate statements
questions.explain: Expressions that mix increment operators with arithmetic are hard to read and easy to get wrong. Write separate statements in the exact order you want. Note that y = x++ + 1; would also compute y from the old x.
